key_insight: MetaboNet consolidates and standardizes multiple public Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) datasets into the largest unified, publicly accessible resource, removing data fragmentation and lowering the barrier for algorithm development and comparison.
problem_solved: Existing T1D datasets are fragmented, heterogeneous in format and metadata, and time-consuming to access and preprocess, which impedes integration, reproducibility, and fair benchmarking of ML algorithms.
method: Aggregate multiple publicly available T1D cohorts and curated sources into a single repository.
Harmonize schema and units (time-series alignment, unified variable names, standardized timestamps) and apply consistent metadata conventions.
Perform quality control, annotate missingness and provenance, and package the consolidated dataset with documentation and easy-to-use formats/APIs for researchers.
impact: MetaboNet reduces preprocessing overhead and enables reproducible benchmarking and cross-cohort validation, accelerating development of more generalizable and robust ML models for T1D management.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: source datasets → cleaning & harmonization → unified MetaboNet release
Stacked bar / donut chart showing dataset composition (CGM, insulin bolus/basal, meals, demographics) by proportion
Example multi-day time-series trace (CGM + insulin events) to illustrate typical inputs for models
Map or icon grid of source datasets with license/status and dataset sizes to show provenance and scale
paper_title: MetaboNet: The Largest Publicly Available Consolidated Dataset for Type 1 Diabetes Management
paper_authors: Miriam K. Wolff, Peter Calhoun, Eleonora Maria Aiello, Yao Qin, Sam F. Royston
